info.title: Melete API
info.description: Media server API for the Melete apps. Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` with every request except the ones marked public. Tokens come from signing in (one per device) or from creating an API key. The web UI signs in to a `melete_session` cookie instead; a request signed in by that cookie that changes something (any method but GET and HEAD) must also send `X-Melete-Web: 1`, or it is refused with 403. Times are Unix seconds. Every error, including malformed requests, has the `Error` shape. Each operation says who may call it in `x-melete-access`: `public` (anyone, no token), `user` (anyone signed in; 401 without a token) or `admin` (admins only; 403 for anyone else signed in). An API key may be limited to what it is for (`KeyScope`): each operation that needs a sign-in says in `x-melete-scope` which scope reaches it, and a key whose scope does not is refused with 403. A `playback` key reaches what a `read` key does; a `full` key or a session reaches everything.

get.summary: Liveness check
This document
Live updates for this device
get.description:
Server-Sent Events, one stream per device, so an app learns of a change as it happens instead of polling. Each kind is sent once at the start and again whenever it changes (looked at every 2 seconds), with keep-alive comments between:

- `sync`: `{"cursor": n}`, the newest change in the Aoide sync log this user would pull (their own, and shared playlists'). Past the device's cursor, pull now (`/aoide/sync/pull`): playlists, likes, the play queue and the rest. With `device`, that device's own pushes aren't counted, so a push isn't echoed back to it.
- `requests`: the user's 50 newest requests, as GET /api/v1/requests lists them, with how each is getting on.
- `library`: counts of `movies`, `episodes`, `albums` and `tracks` with a `version` that changes whenever one is added or goes (Discover may then have changed).
- `scan`: the library scans running now in libraries the user may see, `[{"library", "kind", "whole", "folders_done", "started_at"}]`: the library's name and kind (movies, shows or music), whether it's the whole library or one title folder, the folders read so far (written down once a second while they're walked) and when it started; sent once a scan runs, then as `[]` once none does.
- `favourites`: `{"version": n, "total": n}`, raised by each change to the user's favourite movies and series (GET /api/v1/me/favourites has them); sent once they've had any.
- `pins`: `{"version": n, "items": [{"kind", "id"}]}`, the user's pinned albums, artists and playlists in order (GET /api/v1/music/pins has them in full); sent once they've pinned anything.
- `household`: what everyone else who shares their listening is playing and played lately, as GET /api/v1/music/household lists `people`; sent once anyone else has chosen whether to share.
- `listening`: the listening-together sessions this device is in, as GET /api/v1/music/sessions lists them, whenever one changes; sent once the device is in one, then as `[]` once it's in none.

Only what the way in opens is sent (MELETE_WAYS_IN): `sync`, `pins`, `household` and `listening` with music, `requests` with requests, `favourites` with video, `library` and `scan` with video (movies, episodes, video libraries' scans) or music (albums, tracks, music libraries' scans). The stream ends when its session signs out, and after 10 minutes in any case; EventSource reconnects by itself. Apps keep working by polling when it's down.

get.summary: Download generated bytes, to measure throughput
get.description: Random bytes, as many as asked for (25 MiB by default, 200 MiB at most), with their length up front and never cached; random so no proxy on the way can compress them. Time the download from the first byte to the last. Two tests run at once at most. Opened by every way in, as it measures the way itself.

post.summary: Sign in with username and password
post.description: Returns a session token for this device. It lasts until it is signed out, the password changes, or it goes unused for 90 days. Five attempts per username and address lock that pair for 15 minutes; a wrong password and an unknown username get the same reply. For a user with two-factor sign-in on, a right password answers 401 with a `SecondFactorNeeded` challenge and no token: finish with the code at `/auth/login/second-factor`. A wrong password is answered as for anyone else.

400.description: Bad device name

401.description: Wrong username or password (`Error`), or a right password from a user with two-factor sign-in on (`SecondFactorNeeded`)

post.summary: Sign in to a cookie, for the web UI
post.description: Like `/auth/login`, with the same lockouts, but the session token goes into the `melete_session` cookie instead of the body (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, `Secure` when the request's Origin is https). It lasts as long as a session can go unused, 90 days. With two-factor sign-in on, a right password answers 401 with a `SecondFactorNeeded` challenge and sets no cookie: finish at `/auth/web-login/second-factor`.

400.description: Bad device name

401.description: Wrong username or password (`Error`), or a right password from a user with two-factor sign-in on (`SecondFactorNeeded`)

post.summary: Finish signing in with a second-factor code
post.description: For a user with two-factor sign-in on, `/auth/login` answers a right password with a `SecondFactorNeeded` challenge instead of a token. Send it here with the six-digit code from the user's authenticator app (TOTP: RFC 6238, HMAC-SHA1, 30-second steps; the steps just before and after now are taken too) to get the session the password alone would have given, named with the device name the sign-in started with. A challenge lasts 5 minutes and signs in once; a wrong code leaves it for another try. A code is taken once: never again, nor any code of an earlier step. Each wrong code here is added to the user's own record (`GET /me/two-factor`), without where it came from. Wrong codes count per user, wherever they are typed (here, the web route, confirming setup and turning it off): five lock that user's codes for 15 minutes.

401.description: Wrong code (`reason`: `wrong_code`); the challenge stays usable while it lasts. It's added to the user's record (`GET /me/two-factor`)

410.description: The challenge ran out, was used, was for the other sign-in route or never existed: sign in with the password again

429.description: Too many wrong codes for this user: locked for 15 minutes

post.summary: Finish the web UI's sign-in with a second-factor code
post.description: Like `/auth/login/second-factor`, for a challenge from `/auth/web-login`: the session goes into the `melete_session` cookie, as `/auth/web-login` would have set it. A challenge from one route doesn't finish at the other.

200.description: Signed in; the cookie is set

401.description: Wrong code (`reason`: `wrong_code`); the challenge stays usable while it lasts. It's added to the user's record (`GET /me/two-factor`)

410.description: The challenge ran out, was used, was for the other sign-in route or never existed: sign in with the password again

429.description: Too many wrong codes for this user: locked for 15 minutes

post.summary: End this session
post.description: Revokes the token used for this request, and clears the web UI's cookie.

get.summary: Whether your two-factor sign-in is on
get.description: With your latest changes to it, newest first: turning it on or off, from your account or on the server's command line, and wrong codes typed at sign-in (counted together within an hour of the last; where they were typed from isn't kept), so you can tell if your password is known. Never the secret.

post.summary: Start setting up two-factor sign-in
post.description: Needs your password. Answers a new secret, in base32 for typing in and as an `otpauth://` link for a QR code or a tap, to put in an authenticator app. It is shown only here (never cached), and only until a first code confirms it; starting again before then replaces it. Signing in doesn't change until it's confirmed.

403.description: Wrong password (`reason`: `wrong_password`)

409.description: Two-factor sign-in is on already: turn it off first

429.description: Too many wrong passwords or codes: locked for 15 minutes

post.summary: Turn two-factor sign-in on with a first code
post.description: The six-digit code the authenticator app shows for the secret setup gave. From then on, signing in with the password asks for a code (`/auth/login/second-factor`). Nothing is signed out: sessions and API keys keep working. Quick Connect and signing in through an identity provider don't ask for a code. Wrong codes count as at `/auth/login/second-factor`; a confirm with no setup waiting, or with it on already, answers 409 and doesn't count.

403.description: Wrong code (`reason`: `wrong_code`)

409.description: No setup is waiting for a code, or it's on already

429.description: Too many wrong passwords or codes: locked for 15 minutes

post.summary: Turn two-factor sign-in off
post.description: Needs your password and a current code. Nothing is signed out. Without the device for codes, an admin removes it on the server with `melete user reset-password <name>`, which sets a new password too.

403.description: Wrong password (`reason`: `wrong_password`) or code (`wrong_code`)

409.description: Two-factor sign-in is off already

429.description: Too many wrong passwords or codes: locked for 15 minutes

post.summary: Send a diagnostics report from this device
post.description: Kept 30 days, and at most 100 from one device (the session or API key sending it, by name); older ones go first. Admins read them at `/api/v1/diagnostics`. Put no secrets in a report: anything that looks like one (a value under a key naming a password, token, key, secret, cookie or credential, or a Melete token anywhere in a string) is replaced with `[redacted]` before it's kept. A body over 64 KiB is refused whole.

post.summary: Start Quick Connect on a new device
post.description: For a device where typing a password is a chore (a TV, a new phone). It shows the code; someone signed in elsewhere looks it up (`/auth/quick-connect/lookup`), sees which device it is, and approves it (`/auth/quick-connect/approve`); the device then asks with the secret (`/auth/quick-connect/poll`) and gets a session of its own. Codes last five minutes and are used once. At most five codes wait from one address (an IPv6 /64 counting as one), and a hundred in all, the last twenty kept for requests through a way in that opens everything (the household's own).

400.description: Bad device name

post.summary: Ask whether a Quick Connect code was approved
post.description: Asked every few seconds by the device that started it, with its secret, never the code. Once the code is approved this answers the session, as `/auth/login` does, once; the code is gone after that.

404.description: No such code, or it ran out: start again

post.summary: Look up the code a device shows, before approving it
post.description: Answers which device it is, the address it asked from and how long ago, to check before approving. Each user may look up ten codes an hour, found or not, so codes can't be guessed.

200.description: The device waiting with that code

404.description: No code waiting is that one

429.description: Ten codes looked up this hour

post.summary: Approve the code a device shows
post.description: Signs that device in as you; it appears in your sessions under the name it gave, which this answers. Only a code you've looked up can be approved.

404.description: No code you've looked up is waiting as that one

get.summary: Whether signing in through an identity provider is set up
get.description: For the sign-in page: whether to offer the button, and what to call the provider.

post.summary: Start signing in through the identity provider
post.description: Answers the provider's address to send the browser to. Without `return_to` it's the web UI's sign-in: a cookie ties it to this browser, and the browser comes back to `/#/` with its session cookie set. With `return_to`, an app's: it must be exactly one of the addresses an admin listed (`MELETE_OIDC_APP_RETURNS`; none by default, so apps can't sign in this way until some are), or `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/…` or `http://[::1]:<port>/…` on the device itself. Back from the provider, the browser shows a Melete page asking whether to sign that device in as that user and go back there; on Continue it's sent to `return_to` with `code`, which the app redeems with the `secret` answered here (`/auth/oidc/redeem`). Otherwise it goes back with `error`: `denied` (refused at the provider, or Cancel), `unlinked` (nobody linked that identity), `expired`, `browser` or `failed`. Only an identity a user linked under their account signs in, and only as that user. At most ten sign-ins wait from one address (an IPv6 /64 counting as one) and two hundred in all, the last forty kept for requests through a way in that opens everything (the household's own).

400.description: Bad device name, or a return address no admin listed

502.description: The provider didn't answer as it should

503.description: Signing in through an identity provider isn't set up

get.summary: Where the provider sends the browser back
get.description: Register this address with the provider (`MELETE_OIDC_REDIRECT_URL`). The web UI's sign-in and linking are redirected back to the web UI (`/#/`, or `/#/?oidc=<outcome>` when it didn't work; `/#/settings/account?oidc=linked` after linking). An app's finished sign-in answers a page of Melete's own asking the person in the browser to confirm it (`/auth/oidc/confirm`); anything that went wrong redirects to the app's `return_to` with `error`.

303.description: Back to the web UI or the app

200.description: An app's sign-in, asking to be confirmed

post.summary: Confirm or cancel an app's sign-in, from Melete's confirmation page
post.description: Sent by the confirmation page's form only: it needs the cookie that page set in this browser (SameSite=Strict) and the page's own form token, and works once, within five minutes. Continue sends the browser to the app's `return_to` with `code`; Cancel sends it there with `error=denied`.

400.description: No such sign-in for this browser, or it ran out

503.description: Signing in through an identity provider isn't set up

post.summary: Redeem an app's sign-in for its session
post.description: With the code the app was sent back with and the secret it was given at the start; once, within two minutes. Answers a session as `/auth/login` does.

404.description: No such sign-in, or it ran out

503.description: Signing in through an identity provider isn't set up

get.summary: Whether your account is linked to the identity provider

post.summary: Link your account to your identity at the provider
post.description: Asks for your password again, then answers the provider's address to send this browser to; once you sign in there, that identity signs in as you, in place of any you linked before. An identity linked to someone else isn't moved (`?oidc=taken`). Changing or resetting your password unlinks it. Wrong passwords here count with those of a password change: five stop both for 15 minutes.

429.description: Too many sign-ins under way, or too many wrong passwords

502.description: The provider didn't answer as it should

503.description: Signing in through an identity provider isn't set up

403.description: That isn't your password

post.summary: Find movies or series by describing them
post.description: The description goes to OpenRouter, and nothing else: no titles from the library, nothing about who asked. The model answers with up to 30 titles it knows; those in the library come back in `results` (best fit first, as lists show them), and every suggestion in `suggested`, with its id here or null, so an app can offer to request the rest. A title counts when its title or original title is the suggestion's (case, accents, punctuation and a leading article aside) and its year is at most one off. Each user may search 30 times an hour.

400.description: No description, or one over 300 characters

429.description: Searched 30 times this hour, or OpenRouter is busy

502.description: OpenRouter refused or failed (the key, the account's credit, or the model's answer)

503.description: AI features aren't set up

get.summary: An artwork image
get.description: Use the URLs the other responses return; they never change meaning, so cache them forever. Posters come at w342 or w500, backdrops (textless ones too) at w1280, stills at w300, logos at w500, people's pictures at w185. With `MELETE_DISCOVERY_POSTERS` on, posters of titles not in the library that a discovery answer listed are served too, at w342 only, for 30 days after they were last listed (2000 at most remembered). A title's own poster and backdrop, from its folder (`poster.*` before `folder.*`, `fanart.*` before `backdrop.*`; JPEG, PNG or WebP), are given ahead of TMDB's as `local-<hash>.jpg`, made from the file at the size asked for (JPEG, never wider than the image) and kept; a changed file gets a new name.

parameters.description: TMDB image file name, or a title's own image (`local-<hash>.jpg`).

In autodj mode the chosen records are then ordered as a chain, each next the one the DJ planner scores best from the last (a refused or unread pair counts 0.15). Deterministic: ties break on id. get.description: Every area (movies, series, music, indexers, requests, system, anime), in that order (anime last, after the areas apps knew before it had its own), with its findings: problems first, then what waits for a decision, then notes. A series' findings are under anime when it's anime as the managed lists decide (wanted as anime, or its folder's library, else the library new files go to, has the anime category). Requests waiting for a decision are one finding under requests for all of them, and one under each service (movies, series, anime, music) for its own, as each request's `service` places it. Titles TMDB couldn't settle and no one has decided by hand are a note under their service (titles_unmatched), and a missing TMDB token is a note under system while there are movie or series libraries (tmdb_off). Worked out from the database when asked, from the transcoder's latest GPU test (gpu_unavailable: the GPU is set up but failed its test encode, so video conversions use the CPU), and from TMDB matching's runs since startup (tmdb_refused: TMDB refused the token at the latest run; tmdb_failing: two runs or more in a row got nothing from TMDB, with count the number of runs); nothing outside the server is contacted.

The library task's next run is the next whole scan its schedule (MELETE_SCAN_SCHEDULE) gives; folders imported are scanned at once in between. TMDB matching (tmdb-matching) runs after each scan and when asked, while TMDB is set up; its result counts the titles matched and those that need a match, and says in plain words what went wrong (TMDB refused the token, asked for fewer requests, or no request went through).

Leaving one out works in any season (it counts once the season is monitored); monitoring one needs its season monitored. Set in Melete, an import from Sonarr keeps it until Sonarr's own value for it changes; then Sonarr's, the later change, is taken and followed again. It takes effect at once for searches, RSS syncs and searches for everything missing.

It's remembered with who took it off (/api/v1/wanted/removed), and imports from Radarr, Sonarr and Lidarr and import lists leave it off until it's allowed back or added again there.

Movies and series are looked up on TMDB, music on MusicBrainz. If it can't be added, the removal stays.

A search for a file version and language is sent once a week at most: until then, what it found, nothing included, is given again (remembered). Show the results, then fetch one.

get.summary: What a user can see
get.description: The libraries and highest content rating an admin set for them. Admins see everything whatever is set.

put.summary: Set what a user can see
put.description: Replaces what was set. A movie, series, episode, file, album or track outside it is answered as if it weren't there, by every route: lists, search, details, artwork, streams, subtitles, progress and the apps' routes. With a highest rating, a movie or series is seen only when TMDB gives it a rating Melete can read that comes to that age or under: the rating of the country chosen in Settings (MELETE_RATINGS_COUNTRY, the United States by default), else the United States' rating; episodes go by their series. Movies and series from TMDB's search and discovery that aren't in the library are shown to them only when rated that age or under, their ratings fetched from TMDB by the title's TMDB id and kept a month. Music has no ratings, so only its libraries count; a user who may see only some music libraries gets 403 from Aoide's routes, playlists, listening together, the household's listening and transitions, whose payloads can't be narrowed. Users nobody has restricted see everything, as do admins.

get.summary: A movie's extras
get.description: Trailers, featurettes, behind-the-scenes and other bonus videos in the movie's folder (in folders such as `Trailers/` or `Featurettes/`, or named like `Title-trailer.mkv`), trailers first. They're kept apart from its files, so they never count as the movie itself. Each plays through the file routes by its id; no progress is kept for it.

404.description: No such title, or it's missing

get.summary: A movie's cast, crew and collection
get.description: Its top-billed cast (20 at most, with the characters they play) and key crew (creators, directors and writers), in billing order, from TMDB for titles in the library: fetched after the details, one request a title, and again whenever the details are. Empty while unmatched or not yet fetched. `collection` is the franchise TMDB puts it in.

404.description: No such movie, or it's missing

get.summary: A series's extras
get.description: Trailers, featurettes, behind-the-scenes and other bonus videos in the series's folder (in folders such as `Trailers/` or `Featurettes/`, or named like `Title-trailer.mkv`), trailers first. They're kept apart from its files, so they never count as the series itself. Each plays through the file routes by its id; no progress is kept for it.

404.description: No such title, or it's missing

get.summary: A movie's trailer online
get.description: The trailer chosen from TMDB's video list for the movie, while trailers online is on (MELETE_TRAILERS_ONLINE, off by default): a YouTube trailer or teaser in the metadata language, else English; a trailer before a teaser, an official one before others, then the largest and newest. Play it by loading `embed_url` (YouTube's privacy-enhanced mode, no cookies before playback) in a frame or web view only when the viewer presses play; until then show the title's own backdrop. A trailer in the movie's folder (its extras) comes first. The list is fetched after the movie's details and again whenever they are, so a title can have none yet.

404.description: Trailers online are off, there's no such movie (or it's missing, or hidden from the user), or it has no trailer online

get.summary: A series's trailer online
get.description: As a movie's trailer online, from TMDB's video list for the series.

404.description: Trailers online are off, there's no such series (or it's missing, or hidden from the user), or it has no trailer online

get.summary: A series' cast and crew
get.description: Its top-billed cast (20 at most, with the characters they play) and key crew (creators, directors and writers), in billing order, from TMDB for titles in the library: fetched after the details, one request a title, and again whenever the details are. Empty while unmatched or not yet fetched. `collection` is always null.

404.description: No such series, or it's missing

get.summary: A person and their titles in the library
get.description: Someone credited on a title in the library (kept by TMDB's person id, so two people with one name are two), with each of their titles in the library, newest first, and what they did in it.

404.description: No one by that id is credited on a title in the library

get.summary: A collection's films
get.description: A franchise one of the library's films belongs to, with its films in release order as DiscoverItems. Always those in the library; with `MELETE_DISCOVERY` on, TMDB's collection lookup gives the rest too (`all_films`), marked requested or requestable. Only the collection's id leaves the server.

404.description: No film in the library belongs to it

202.description: Asked for; it runs at once unless a scan is running, then right after

202.description: Asked for; it runs at once unless a scan is running, then right after

added_at.description: When it was put on the wanted list, else when its first file was found; Unix seconds.

download.description: A download under way for it (an upgrade too).

cutoff_unmet.description: Whether its file is below its profile's cutoff, so an upgrade is looked for: the profile upgrades, and the best of the files an upgrade would be compared with (those of the folder linked to the wanted entry) ranks below the cutoff's quality or scores below the upgrade-until score, chosen and judged exactly as searches and RSS judge upgrades. For a series, true when any monitored episode's is. Null when it isn't judged: not monitored, no file in the linked folder, no profile here, or a file whose quality can't be told yet; always null for artists, as music isn't upgraded.

artist_id.description: The artist in the music library (see GET /api/v1/music/artists/{id}).

monitor_new.description: What happens to albums they release later; null when not wanted.

albums_on_disk.description: Of the monitored albums that are out, those on disk; for an artist who isn't wanted, every album of theirs on disk.

albums_wanted.description: Monitored albums that are out (none when the artist isn't monitored).

title.description: As it was called then; for music, the album or song with its artist.

season.description: For a series, when it was for one season.

search_id.description: The search, while it's kept (30 days).

release.description: The release or file involved: for a rename, the new file; for an extra, its file.

message.description: The latest word on it: a search's result count, a download's source, why it failed, what replaced a file, an extra's kind, or the file a renamed one took the place of.

album.description: For an artist: the album searched for.

rss.description: Whether an RSS sync made it.

since.description: The day of the first look (YYYY-MM-DD); null until one is made.

checked_at.description: When the last look was made, unix seconds; null until one is.

error.description: Why the last look failed, when it did.

removed.description: How many failed downloads were removed.

monitor_new.description: What happens to albums they release later.

goal.description: What the run searches for: what's missing (POST /api/v1/missing-searches), or upgrades of what's below its cutoff (POST /api/v1/cutoff-searches).

state.description: stopping: asked to stop, finishing the search under way. stopped: asked to, or an indexer reached its limit, or none is turned on (see message).

total.description: Searches the run set out to make (a series counts each season); 0 until it has worked out what's missing.

done.description: How many of those it has dealt with, searched for or not (one found meanwhile is passed over).

grabbed.description: Searches a release was grabbed from.

current.description: What it's searching for now, while running.

message.description: How it ended: what was searched for and grabbed, or why it stopped or failed.

notes.description: Why some weren't searched for or grabbed ("Title: why"), the first 50.

started_by.description: The username of the admin who started it; null once that account is gone.

key.description: What imports know it by: a movie's TMDB id, a series' TVDB id, an artist's or album's MusicBrainz id.

removed_by.description: The username of the admin who took it off; null when unknown (taken off before this was kept, or the account is gone).

key.description: What imports know it by: a movie's TMDB id, a series' TVDB id, an artist's or album's MusicBrainz id.

wanted_id.description: Its id on the wanted list of its kind (/api/v1/wanted/movies, series, artists or albums).

results.description: Made for this very file first, then the most downloaded; 20 at most.

release.description: The release it was made for, as its uploader named it.

matches_file.description: Made for this very file: its hash matched.

remembered.description: Given from a search sent in the last week, rather than asked again.

fetched.description: The subtitle fetched for this language already, if any.

estimated_bytes.description: About how big it will be, worked out when asked for.

bytes.description: How big it is, once ready.

delete_at.description: When it will be deleted: 7 days after the last download (or after it was made), a day after failing; null while waiting or being made.

height.description: Each picture's height in pixels, in the video's shape.

times.description: Each picture's time in seconds, in order. Picture i is on sheet i / (columns × rows), at column i % columns and row (i / columns) % rows. Show the last picture at or before the time under the pointer.

name.description: The name as credited on this track, which can differ from the artist's.

id.description: Plays through the file routes (`/files/{id}`, `/play`, `/transcode`, `/subtitles`) like a file's id; no progress or watched state is kept for it.

name.description: As TMDB names it.

embed_url.description: https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/ and the key: the only address to load it from. Add player parameters (such as autoplay=1) as needed.

job.description: Creator, Director, Screenplay, Writer, Story, Novel or Teleplay.

id.description: The movie's or series' id in the library.

all_films.description: Whether TMDB was asked for the films not in the library (`MELETE_DISCOVERY` on); otherwise only those in it are listed.

admin.description: An admin sees everything, whatever is set.

libraries.description: The libraries they can see, by name; null for every library, those added later too.

max_age.description: The highest age a movie or series may be rated for; null for no limit.

libraries.description: Library names; null for every library, those added later too.

total.description: How many there are of the kind asked for.

version.description: Raised by each change to your favourites; 0 when you've never had any.

present.description: Whether the title is in the library now.

added_at.description: Unix seconds; null when it isn't a favourite.

TrackPick.description: Every app playing the file for this user picks these. Untagged tracks never count as being in a language; a language with a region (`pt-BR`) is never taken for another region of it, and a track naming no region comes after one naming the same region.

audio.description: The audio stream's index, as in the file's `media.audio`; null for a file without audio.

audio_reason.description: `series_choice`: in the language last chosen by hand in this series. `preferred_language`: the first of your audio languages the file has. `file_default`: none of them is there, so the file's default (else its first).

subtitle.description: The track as the file's subtitle list names it (`s3`, `x1a2b3c4d`); null for none.

subtitle_reason.description: `series_choice`: like the subtitles last chosen by hand in this series, or off because they were turned off there. `always`: full subtitles in your first subtitle language the file has. `foreign_audio`: the same, because the audio isn't in one of your subtitle languages (or isn't tagged). `forced`: forced subtitles (the parts in another language) in one of your subtitle languages, else the audio's. `off`: your subtitle mode is off. `audio_understood`: the audio is in one of your subtitle languages and there are no forced ones. `no_match`: nothing in your languages.

subtitle_languages.description: Most wanted first. Audio in one of these is taken as understood.

subtitle_mode.description: `off`: none, forced ones included. `forced`: only forced ones. `foreign`: full subtitles when the audio isn't in one of your subtitle languages, else forced ones. `always`: full subtitles.

audio_language.description: The chosen audio's language tag as the file gives it; null when it has none, and nothing is remembered about the audio.

subtitle.description: null when subtitles were turned off.

language.description: The track's language tag; null when it has none, and nothing is remembered about the subtitles.
